extracted.intended_audience: writers and publishing professionals interested in HWA membership and Bram Stoker Award participation
extracted.subtask_short: HWA Bram Stoker award and membership rules
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Horror Writers Association's membership categories, organizational standards, and the basic eligibility/intent of the Bram Stoker Awards (what they recognize and the Lifetime Achievement award). Useful for prospective members and entrants to understand who may join, who votes, and what the awards honor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bram Stoker Awards — scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bram Stoker Awards® are presented for superior writing in eleven categories including traditional fiction of various lengths, poetry, screenwriting, graphic novels, young adult, and non-fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named in honor of Bram Stoker, the awards recognize 'superior achievement in horror literature' across multiple formats; categories cover a range of lengths and media (fiction, poetry, screenwriting, graphic novels, YA, non-fiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifetime Achievement Award — eligibility criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual Lifetime Achievement Award is presented to a living person who has made significant contributions to the writing of Horror and Dark Fantasy over the course of a lifetime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This award honors long-term, significant contributions to horror/dark fantasy writing; recipient must be living.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active (voting) membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: HWA’s Active (voting) members are all published professional writers of horror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active membership is reserved for established professional writers; Active members have voting rights (implied in 'voting' membership label).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate membership — demonstration of intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliate-level membership requires demonstrated intention to become a professional writer; 'all you need is one minimally paid publication in any of several categories.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: this might be a 500-word story for which you’ve received $25 or more. The Affiliate level is intended for those who are not yet established professionals but show intent toward a professional career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate membership — non-writer professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-writing professionals with an interest in the field (such as illustrators, librarians, booksellers, producers, agents, editors, and teachers) can join at the Associate level without any publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate membership enables industry-adjacent professionals to participate in HWA without meeting publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting membership — benefits and privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting Membership is for non-professionals who would like to share and explore their interest in horror; supporting members receive HWA’s monthly newsletter and internet mailers and have the opportunity to recommend works for the Bram Stoker Awards®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting members may also be involved with HWA chapters, the Mentor Program, and gain access to a private message board; the page explicitly notes the ability to recommend works for the awards as a supporting-member privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-harassment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: HWA is dedicated to recognizing and promoting diversity in the horror genre, and practices a strict anti-harassment policy at all of its events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational standard applying to events and community conduct; tied to HWA’s commitment to diversity and safe participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational mission — promotion of dark literature
rubrics_metrics.description: One of HWA’s missions is to encourage public interest in and foster an appreciation of good Horror and Dark Fantasy literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities to accomplish this include public website content, readings and lectures, blog publication, materials for booksellers/librarians, participation at conventions, facilitating readings/signings, and maintaining an official presence at major fan conventions.
